steps.do: Before you start: start the stand-in gateway (assets/server/llm_gateway.py) and a stack as the README describes (--real-llm, CALIBER_GATEWAY_URI and CALIBER_LLM_BASE_URL pointing at it, the deliberately wrong boot key). Open LLM Gateway and read the Endpoints tab.
steps.see: Reachable, Through gateway, and two endpoint rows: chat-lab and embeddings-lab.

steps.do: Pause the stand-in (curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8791/admin/pause) and refresh the page; then resume it and refresh again.
steps.see: Unreachable with the discovery error while paused -- a degraded card, never a broken page -- then Reachable again.

steps.do: Import assets/workflow/metered-reply.workflow.yaml, publish it, and run it once while the provider key is still the wrong boot key.
steps.see: The run ends error with the gateway's own 401 in the message, and the gateway's ledger records one refused call.

steps.do: As an admin, write the right provider key at runtime (PATCH /settings/llm {"openai_api_key": ...}; the Settings page's LLM section is the same surface). An operator gets 403.
steps.see: The masked fingerprint (•••• + the key's last 4) confirms which key is live; the value itself is never readable back.

steps.do: Click Add rate and price the gateway's model: provider lab, model lab-chat-mini, $1/1K prompt, $2/1K completion.
steps.see: The rate row appears. A duplicate (provider, model) is refused with 409, and editing a rate is admin-only.

steps.do: Run the metered workflow again, now on the right key.
steps.see: The run completes with the gateway model's reply, and the gateway's ledger records one real call billing a flat 1000+1000 tokens.

steps.do: Open the Usage tab and find lab-chat-mini in the by-model table.
steps.see: One more call, 2000 more tokens, and exactly $3.00 more cost: (1000/1000)×$1 + (1000/1000)×$2.

steps.do: Raise the prompt rate to $10/1K (admin), re-read Usage, then run the workflow once more.
steps.see: Past cost is unchanged -- the meter is written at call time -- and the new call bills $12.00.

steps.do: Store the gateway key under a name (Store / rotate), then store it again with a new value.
steps.see: The listing shows the name, a bumped version and a secret:// reference -- never a value. A secret:// source for CALIBER_LLM_API_KEY_ENV resolves from this store at boot.

steps.do: Click New guardrail, pick the deterministic regex kind, name it, set a pattern, create it -- then delete it.
steps.see: The definition is listed (stored in the MLflow tracking store). Enforcement happens in MLflow's own AI Gateway, not in the standalone gateway the Endpoints tab lists -- the lab is explicit about that boundary.
